title: ACCY 6100 — Auditing Seminar
subtitle: Audit test 3
source: Practice exam for Modules 9–14 plus 50 bonus questions (188 one-best-answer and 62 select-all)

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: Which statement best describes audit evidence?

choices.text: Only the documents the client gives the auditor
All the information used by the auditor to reach the conclusions on which the opinion is based
Only the workpapers kept in the audit file

questions.explanation: Correct: C. Evidence is all information used to reach the conclusions underlying the opinion.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: Evidence sufficiency is a measure of the:
questions.explanation: Correct: A. Sufficiency is quantity.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: Evidence appropriateness consists of:
questions.explanation: Correct: D. Appropriateness = relevance + reliability.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: As the assessed risk of material misstatement (RMM) increases, the auditor should:

choices.text: Obtain less evidence because controls are weak
Reduce the extent of substantive testing

questions.explanation: Correct: B. Higher RMM calls for more persuasive evidence.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: All else equal, as the quality of the evidence collected increases, the quantity of corroborating evidence needed:
questions.explanation: Correct: C. Better quality means less corroboration needed.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: (Select ALL that apply.) The reliability of audit evidence depends on the source of the evidence, including the level of the source’s:

choices.text: Number of pages in the document

questions.explanation: Correct: A,B. Reliability depends on source bias and competence.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: Which evidence is generally MOST reliable?

choices.text: A spreadsheet prepared by the controller
A bank statement received directly from the bank
An oral explanation from the CFO
A photocopy of a bank statement from the client’s files

questions.explanation: Correct: B. Evidence received directly from an independent third party is most reliable.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: (Select ALL that apply.) Which are appropriate overall audit responses to assessed risks of material misstatement (AS 2301)?

choices.text: Reduce professional skepticism to save time
Evaluate the selection and application of accounting principles

questions.explanation: Correct: A,B,C,E. Skepticism must not be reduced.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: Which is the best example of building unpredictability into an audit?

choices.text: Testing the same accounts at the same threshold each year
Announcing site visits to client managers
Varying the timing, locations, and testing thresholds, and testing items not usually tested
Reusing last year’s audit program unchanged

questions.explanation: Correct: C. Vary timing, locations, thresholds.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT a substantive procedure?
questions.explanation: Correct: C. Tests of controls are not substantive.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: (Select ALL that apply.) Substantive procedures include:
questions.explanation: Correct: A,B,C. Tests of details and substantive AP.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: Which of the following is a test of details?

choices.text: Comparing gross margin percentage with the industry average
Reviewing the trend in days sales outstanding
Inquiring of the CFO about changes in revenue
Vouching a sample of PP&E additions to vendor invoices

questions.explanation: Correct: D. Vouching individual items is a test of details.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: In the expanded audit risk model, audit risk (AuR) equals:
questions.explanation: Correct: C. AuR = IR × CR × AP × TD.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: The auditor will accept audit risk of 5%. IR = 100%, CR = 50%, and AP risk = 80%. What is the acceptable risk for tests of details (TD)?

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: AuR = 4%, IR = 80%, CR = 50%, AP risk = 50%. What is the acceptable TD risk?

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: Tests of details risk (TD) is the probability that the auditor’s tests of details will NOT detect a material misstatement that:

choices.text: Occurred, was not prevented or detected by ICFR, and was not detected by substantive analytical procedures
Occurred and was detected by ICFR

questions.explanation: Correct: A. TD risk definition.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: (Select ALL that apply.) Circumstances favoring the use of confirmations (AS 2310) rather than evidence from the client include:

choices.text: Evidence is already available from the client at low risk
The client prefers not to contact third parties

questions.explanation: Correct: A,B. Higher RMM and complex transactions.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: A confirmation is:

choices.text: A client-prepared schedule agreed to the ledger
A direct communication from a third party in response to a request for information about an item affecting the financial statements
A recalculation of a balance by the auditor

questions.explanation: Correct: C. Confirmation = direct third-party communication.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: For accounts receivable, confirmations are LEAST useful for testing:

choices.text: None; confirmations address all assertions equally well

questions.explanation: Correct: C. Confirmations do not address valuation/collectibility well.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: (Select ALL that apply.) Confirmations are generally NOT as useful for testing which assertions?
questions.explanation: Correct: B,C,D. Valuation, completeness, presentation and disclosure.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: A positive confirmation:

choices.text: Asks the recipient to respond whether or not they agree
Asks the recipient to respond only if they disagree
Is never used for accounts receivable
Provides no evidence even when answered

questions.explanation: Correct: A. Positive asks for a response in all cases.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: The auditor does not receive a response to a positive confirmation. The non-response:

choices.text: Is evidence the balance is correct
Is evidence the balance is overstated
Provides no evidence by itself, so alternative procedures are needed

questions.explanation: Correct: D. Non-response is no evidence; do alternative procedures.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: For a negative confirmation, a non-response:

choices.text: Provides some evidence (the recipient did not disagree)
Must always be followed by a second request

questions.explanation: Correct: C. Negative non-response gives some evidence.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: (Select ALL that apply.) Negative confirmations are most appropriate when:

choices.text: There are a large number of small balances
There are a few large balances
The auditor has no reason to believe recipients will disregard the request

questions.explanation: Correct: A,B,D. Low risk, many small balances, recipients expected to respond.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: A client has 8 customers with very large receivable balances and RMM is high. The best confirmation approach is:
questions.explanation: Correct: A. Few large balances and high risk call for positives.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: A utility has 50,000 small residential balances, strong controls, and low assessed risk. The most efficient approach is likely:

choices.text: Negative confirmations (possibly with positives for larger balances)

questions.explanation: Correct: C. Many small balances and low risk suit negatives.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: The client controller offers to mail the confirmations to save the auditor time. The auditor should:

choices.text: Accept, since the controller knows the customers
Accept if the controller signs a representation
Decline; the auditor must control the mailing and receipt

questions.explanation: Correct: D. The auditor must control mailing.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: A confirmation reply shows a balance different from the client’s records. The auditor should:

choices.text: Adjust the ledger to the confirmation amount
Investigate and perform alternative procedures to determine the cause (e.g., timing differences vs. misstatement)

questions.explanation: Correct: B. Investigate differences with alternative procedures.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: (Select ALL that apply.) Appropriate alternative procedures when a customer does not respond to a positive receivable confirmation include:

choices.text: Examining customer purchase orders or sales contracts
Accepting management’s assurance that the balance is valid
Removing the account from the population

questions.explanation: Correct: A,B,C. Subsequent receipts, shipping documents, customer orders.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: Observation of the client’s inventory count is best described as a:
questions.explanation: Correct: C. Dual-purpose (control and detail).

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: (Select ALL that apply.) Purposes of an inventory observation include:

choices.text: Evaluating the effectiveness of the client’s inventory-taking procedures
Verifying existence by counting and examining a sample of items
Testing valuation by obtaining market price quotes
Verifying that the client has a perpetual system

questions.explanation: Correct: A,B. Evaluate count procedures and verify existence.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: The client uses a perpetual system with cycle counts rather than a year-end count. The auditor:

choices.text: Does not need to observe any counts
Should be present when the cycle counts are performed
May rely on the client’s counts without observation
Should only review the count sheets afterward

questions.explanation: Correct: B. Be present at cycle counts.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: Audit documentation is best defined as:

choices.text: The written record of the basis for the auditor’s conclusions that supports the auditor’s representations

questions.explanation: Correct: D. Documentation definition.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: (Select ALL that apply.) Audit documentation might be reviewed by:
questions.explanation: Correct: A,B,C,D. Not competitors.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: Which statement best distinguishes evidence from documentation?

choices.text: Documentation is information obtained from third parties; evidence is the audit file
Evidence is the information the auditor obtains through procedures; documentation is the written record of the basis for the conclusions
Evidence is only oral; documentation is only written

questions.explanation: Correct: C. Evidence = information; documentation = record of the basis.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: (Select ALL that apply.) Examples of audit documentation include:

choices.text: Management’s internal strategy memo that the auditor never received

questions.explanation: Correct: A,B,C,D. Items never received are not audit documentation.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: (Select ALL that apply.) According to PCAOB standards, audit documentation should:

choices.text: Demonstrate the engagement complied with PCAOB standards
Support the basis for conclusions on every relevant financial statement assertion
Demonstrate the accounting records agree or can be reconciled with the financial statements
Show that management agrees with each conclusion
Guarantee that all misstatements were detected

questions.explanation: Correct: A,B,C. Demonstrate the engagement complied with PCAOB standards; Support the basis for conclusions on every relevant financial statement assertion; Demonstrate the accounting records agree or can be reconciled with the financial statements

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: The auditor must retain audit documentation for:

choices.text: Five years from the audit report date
Seven years from the date the auditor grants permission to use the report
Ten years from the date fieldwork began

questions.explanation: Correct: C. Seven years from permission to use the report.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: If no audit report is issued, documentation must be retained for seven years from:

choices.text: The date the engagement letter was signed
The date of the client’s next audit

questions.explanation: Correct: A. Seven years from fieldwork completion.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: If the engagement is not completed, documentation is retained for seven years from the date:
questions.explanation: Correct: D. Seven years from when the engagement ceased.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: During the retention period, a senior wants to delete an outdated workpaper and attach a new memo. Under PCAOB rules the auditor:

choices.text: May add documentation but may not remove existing workpapers

questions.explanation: Correct: B. May add, may not remove.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: Audit sampling is the application of an audit procedure to:

choices.text: Less than 100% of the items in a balance or class, expecting the sample to be representative

questions.explanation: Correct: A. Less than 100% and representative.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: (Select ALL that apply.) Procedures that likely do NOT involve sampling include:

choices.text: Automated application controls when general IT controls are effective
A test of details of receivables on a selected subset

questions.explanation: Correct: A,B,C,D. Inquiry and observation; Analytical procedures; Testing every item using CAATs; Automated application controls when general IT controls are effective

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: Sampling is typically used in:

choices.text: Some tests of (manual) controls, some substantive tests, and some dual-purpose tests

questions.explanation: Correct: C. Some tests of (manual) controls, some substantive tests, and some dual-purpose tests

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: The risk of incorrect acceptance is the risk of:

choices.text: Concluding a material misstatement does not exist when it does (or controls are more effective than they are)
Concluding a misstatement exists when it does not

questions.explanation: Correct: A. Incorrect acceptance (over-reliance).

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: The risk of under-reliance on controls corresponds to the risk of:
questions.explanation: Correct: D. Under-reliance = incorrect rejection.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: (Select ALL that apply.) Benefits of statistical sampling include helping the auditor:

choices.text: Measure the sufficiency of the evidence obtained

questions.explanation: Correct: A,B,C. Statistical sampling does not eliminate sampling or non-sampling risk.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: A downside of statistical sampling is that it:
questions.explanation: Correct: D. Needs specialized knowledge.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: An auditor wants a conclusion about the rate of exceptions in approving vouchers (a control). The appropriate approach is:
questions.explanation: Correct: B. Rate of deviation = attributes.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: An auditor wants a conclusion about the dollar amount of existing receivables. The appropriate approach is:
questions.explanation: Correct: A. Dollar amounts = variables.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: In attributes sampling, each deviation is:

choices.text: Weighted by the size of the population
Given equal weight regardless of the dollar amount of the transaction
Ignored if the transaction is small

questions.explanation: Correct: C. Deviations weighted equally.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: In attributes sampling, as the tolerable rate of deviation increases, the sample size:
questions.explanation: Correct: D. Higher tolerable rate means smaller sample.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: As the expected population deviation rate increases, the attributes sample size:
questions.explanation: Correct: A. Higher expected deviation means larger sample.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: (Select ALL that apply.) Which changes would INCREASE an attributes sample size?

choices.text: Expected deviation rate raised from 1% to 3%
Acceptable risk of over-reliance lowered from 10% to 5%

questions.explanation: Correct: A,B,C,D. Only a higher tolerable rate (E) would decrease it.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: In a variables test, as tolerable misstatement increases, the sample size:
questions.explanation: Correct: C. Decreases

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: As expected misstatement approaches tolerable misstatement, the required sample size:

choices.text: Increases, because more precise measurement is needed

questions.explanation: Correct: A. Increases, because more precise measurement is needed

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: Population size has what effect on the sample size in a variables test?

choices.text: Little effect unless the population is very small

questions.explanation: Correct: D. Little effect unless the population is very small

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: The auditor accepts a higher AP risk (analytical procedures provide less assurance). The acceptable TD risk:
questions.explanation: Correct: B. Acceptable TD falls, so samples grow.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: Which selection method gives larger items a higher probability of selection and increases dollar coverage?
questions.explanation: Correct: C. PPS.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: The auditor selects items without conscious bias but without a randomizing device. This is:
questions.explanation: Correct: A. Haphazard.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: A sample of $10,000 contains $500 of misstatement. The population is $400,000. Projecting proportionally, the estimated misstatement is:

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: The auditor cannot apply the planned procedure to a selected item (e.g., the invoice cannot be located). The auditor should:

choices.text: Consider the reasons and perform alternative procedures

questions.explanation: Correct: D. Consider reasons and use alternative procedures.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: The auditor selects every 10th vendor invoice beginning with the 3rd. Documentation should include:

choices.text: The source of the documents, the starting point, and the sampling interval

questions.explanation: Correct: B. Source, starting point (3rd), interval (10).

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: The auditor selects all vendor invoices over $1,000. Documentation need only describe:

choices.text: The dollar scope and the population the items were drawn from

questions.explanation: Correct: C. Dollar scope and population.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: The auditor selects a sample from a population of documents. Documentation should include:

choices.text: Identifying characteristics of each item selected

questions.explanation: Correct: A. Identifying characteristics of each item selected

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: The AICPA’s detailed audit guide covering statistical and non-statistical sampling was published in:
questions.explanation: Correct: D. 1983.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: Statistical sampling requires the sample to be:
questions.explanation: Correct: B. Representative (random).

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: In substantive testing, the “precision required” is the difference between:
questions.explanation: Correct: C. Expected vs. tolerable misstatement.

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: (Select ALL that apply.) Planning a sample for a substantive test of details includes:

choices.text: Defining the population (and checking its completeness)
Defining the sampling unit and identifying individually significant items
Choosing a statistical or non-statistical technique
Eliminating all sampling risk before testing

questions.explanation: Correct: A,B,C,D. Determining the test objectives; Defining the population (and checking its completeness); Defining the sampling unit and identifying individually significant items; Choosing a statistical or non-statistical technique

questions.module: Module 9: Evidence, Confirmations, Inventory, Documentation, Sampling
questions.prompt: (Select ALL that apply.) Which are examples of NON-sampling risk?

choices.text: Using an inappropriate audit procedure for the objective
Failing to recognize a misstatement in a document examined
Selecting too small a sample for the desired confidence
A random sample that happens to be unrepresentative
A properly selected sample that, by chance, differs from the population

questions.explanation: Correct: A,B. C and D describe sampling risk.

questions.prompt: Analytical procedures are evaluations of financial information made by studying:

choices.text: Plausible relationships among financial and nonfinancial data

questions.explanation: Correct: C. Plausible relationships among financial and nonfinancial data

questions.prompt: Which best distinguishes tests of details from analytical procedures?

choices.text: Tests of details study relationships; analytical procedures examine individual items
Tests of details examine the individual elements of a balance or class; analytical procedures evaluate relationships among data
Only analytical procedures can be substantive

questions.explanation: Correct: B. Tests of details examine the individual elements of a balance or class; analytical procedures evaluate relationships among data

questions.prompt: Which is a substantive analytical procedure?

choices.text: Predicting interest expense from average debt × stated rate and comparing it to the recorded amount

questions.explanation: Correct: D. An expectation compared with the recorded amount.

questions.prompt: (Select ALL that apply.) Analytical procedures are used in which phases of the audit?

choices.text: Planning, to help understand the client’s business and identify risk areas
Wrap-up, to assess consistency of the statements with the auditor’s understanding of the entity
Only after the opinion has been issued
As a replacement for audit documentation

questions.explanation: Correct: A,B,C. Planning, to help understand the client’s business and identify risk areas; Fieldwork, as a substantive procedure; Wrap-up, to assess consistency of the statements with the auditor’s understanding of the entity

questions.prompt: The correct order of steps in an analytical procedure is:

choices.text: Develop an expectation, compare to the recorded amount, investigate differences, document
Compare, develop an expectation, document, investigate
Document, develop an expectation, compare, investigate
Investigate, compare, develop an expectation, document

questions.explanation: Correct: A. Develop an expectation, compare to the recorded amount, investigate differences, document

questions.prompt: The most critical element of a substantive analytical procedure is:
questions.explanation: Correct: C. Precision.

questions.prompt: (Select ALL that apply.) Precision of an expectation depends on:

choices.text: The sophistication (type) of the expectation developed
The reliability of the data used
The objectivity (nature) of the account or assertion
The size of the audit fee

questions.explanation: Correct: A,B,C. The sophistication (type) of the expectation developed; The reliability of the data used; The objectivity (nature) of the account or assertion

questions.prompt: Which expectation is likely MORE precise?

choices.text: An asset recorded at an estimated fair value

questions.explanation: Correct: A. Objective, fixed-rate items give precise expectations.

questions.prompt: As the auditor needs more assurance from the analytical procedure (lower AP risk), the auditor should:

choices.text: Demand more precision in the expectation

questions.explanation: Correct: D. Demand more precision in the expectation

questions.prompt: Trend analysis is most appropriate when:

choices.text: Amounts are expected to be stable and the environment is relatively unchanged

questions.explanation: Correct: B. Amounts are expected to be stable and the environment is relatively unchanged

questions.prompt: Which trend analysis is likely MORE precise?

choices.text: A one-year change in total assets

questions.explanation: Correct: C. Lower aggregation is more precise.

questions.prompt: An auditor predicts hotel room revenue as rooms × occupancy rate × average daily rate. This is:

choices.text: A ratio analysis with implicit expectations

questions.explanation: Correct: D. Reasonableness test (explicit).

questions.prompt: Which method provides statistical measures of the precision of the expectation?
questions.explanation: Correct: C. Regression.

questions.prompt: (Select ALL that apply.) Advantages of regression analysis include:

choices.text: It can produce more precise expectations
It requires no understanding of the relationships involved
It guarantees the recorded amount is correct

questions.explanation: Correct: A,B,C. It can incorporate multiple factors; It provides measures of precision; It can produce more precise expectations

questions.prompt: Which approach involves implicit expectations rather than explicit predictions?
questions.explanation: Correct: A. Trend and ratio analysis rely on implicit expectations.

questions.prompt: The auditor decides whether a difference between the expectation and the recorded amount is significant by reference to:
questions.explanation: Correct: B. Materiality thresholds.

questions.prompt: Bad debt expense is unexpectedly low, and management says credit policies were tightened. The best next step is to:

choices.text: Corroborate the explanation (e.g., review the new policy, its approval, and evidence of implementation; inquire of independent parties)

questions.explanation: Correct: D. Corroborate management’s explanation.

questions.prompt: The more precise the auditor’s expectation, the more likely a difference is due to:

choices.text: Misstatement rather than other potential explanations

questions.explanation: Correct: A. Misstatement rather than other potential explanations

questions.prompt: (Select ALL that apply.) To evaluate plausible non-misstatement explanations for differences, the auditor should consider:

choices.text: Inquiries of independent parties (inside and outside the company)
Management’s explanation alone, if it sounds reasonable

questions.explanation: Correct: A,B,C. Inquiries of independent parties (inside and outside the company); Evidence from other audit procedures; Evidence from other supporting documentation

questions.prompt: Documentation of a substantive analytical procedure should include:

choices.text: The expectation and factors considered, the comparison results, and any additional procedures and their results

questions.explanation: Correct: C. The expectation and factors considered, the comparison results, and any additional procedures and their results

questions.prompt: (Select ALL that apply.) Plausible explanations for a significant difference between expectation and recorded amount include:

choices.text: Unusual events or changes in business or accounting processes
Unreliable data used to form the expectation

questions.explanation: Correct: A,B,C,D. Inherent factors affecting the account; Unusual events or changes in business or accounting processes; Unreliable data used to form the expectation; An actual misstatement

questions.prompt: An auditor predicts revenue by multiplying last year’s revenue by 1.03 without considering that the client opened five new stores. The main problem is:

choices.text: The procedure is not a test of details
The expectation ignores known factors, so it lacks the precision needed for substantive assurance
A test of controls is required instead

questions.explanation: Correct: B. Ignores new stores, so too imprecise.

questions.prompt: (Select ALL that apply.) Auditors or management may use specialists for:

choices.text: Determining amounts derived using specialized techniques
Deciding which audit opinion to issue

questions.explanation: Correct: A,B,C,D. Valuation; Determining physical characteristics; Determining amounts derived using specialized techniques; Technical interpretations

questions.prompt: For which situation is a specialist MOST likely needed?

choices.text: Valuing complex derivatives or mineral reserves

questions.explanation: Correct: C. Valuing complex derivatives or mineral reserves

questions.prompt: Which standard governs the use of a specialist ENGAGED by the auditor?
questions.explanation: Correct: C. AS 1210.

questions.prompt: A specialist EMPLOYED by the audit firm is treated under:
questions.explanation: Correct: B. AS 1201.

questions.prompt: A specialist employed or engaged by the CLIENT is addressed in:
questions.explanation: Correct: A. AS 1105, App. A.

questions.prompt: (Select ALL that apply.) When the auditor engages a specialist, the auditor should assess the specialist’s:

choices.text: Certification, licensing, or accreditation in the field
Experience with the type of work

questions.explanation: Correct: A,B,C,D. Knowledge, skill, and ability; Objectivity; Certification, licensing, or accreditation in the field; Experience with the type of work

questions.prompt: Which is NOT a factor in assessing a specialist’s qualifications?

choices.text: Experience with the type of work
A financial relationship with the client

questions.explanation: Correct: D. That is an objectivity factor.

questions.prompt: The specialist’s employer has a significant financial relationship with the client. The auditor is mainly concerned with the specialist’s:
questions.explanation: Correct: C. Objectivity.

questions.prompt: (Select ALL that apply.) Information that helps the auditor assess a specialist’s objectivity includes:

choices.text: Written representations or disclosures in the specialist’s report

questions.explanation: Correct: A,B,C,D. Related-party information; Employment contracts; Questionnaire responses; Written representations or disclosures in the specialist’s report

questions.prompt: (Select ALL that apply.) The auditor should inform an engaged specialist of:

choices.text: The degree of responsibility for testing data, evaluating assumptions or developing their own, and evaluating methods
The specialist’s reporting responsibilities (work, results, conclusions)
The auditor’s personal opinion about management’s honesty

questions.explanation: Correct: A,B,C,D. The specialist’s responsibilities; The nature of the work; The degree of responsibility for testing data, evaluating assumptions or developing their own, and evaluating methods; The specialist’s reporting responsibilities (work, results, conclusions)

questions.prompt: In addition to describing the work, the auditor should give the specialist:

choices.text: Information about the client and its environment that could affect the specialist’s work

questions.explanation: Correct: B. Information about the client and its environment that could affect the specialist’s work

questions.prompt: Evaluating an engaged specialist’s work includes reviewing the report to determine there is sufficient appropriate evidence that:

choices.text: The work took less than a month
The work was performed as agreed and the conclusions are consistent with the work and other audit evidence

questions.explanation: Correct: D. The work was performed as agreed and the conclusions are consistent with the work and other audit evidence

questions.prompt: The extent of review of the specialist’s work depends on:

choices.text: The degree of reliance on the specialist, the risk of material misstatement, and the specialist’s knowledge, skill, and ability

questions.explanation: Correct: A. The degree of reliance on the specialist, the risk of material misstatement, and the specialist’s knowledge, skill, and ability

questions.prompt: The auditor relies heavily on a specialist for a high-risk assertion, and the specialist has limited experience. The review should be:
questions.explanation: Correct: C. More extensive review.

questions.prompt: The key difference between an auditor-employed specialist and an engaged specialist is that the employed specialist:

choices.text: Is not subject to any oversight
Is a member of the audit team and is supervised under AS 1201
May not be used for valuation

questions.explanation: Correct: B. Is a member of the audit team and is supervised under AS 1201

questions.prompt: For an auditor-employed specialist, the engagement partner must:

choices.text: Inform the specialist of the work, provide client information, and evaluate whether the work complies with instructions and the conclusions are consistent with other evidence
Have the client supervise the work

questions.explanation: Correct: A. Inform the specialist of the work, provide client information, and evaluate whether the work complies with instructions and the conclusions are consistent with other evidence

questions.prompt: For a specialist employed or engaged by the client, evaluating the work (AS 1105, App. A) includes testing:

choices.text: The accuracy of the data used, the reasonableness of significant assumptions, and the appropriateness of the methods
Nothing; the work may be accepted as is

questions.explanation: Correct: C. Data, assumptions, methods.

questions.prompt: Why is objectivity especially important for a client-employed specialist?

choices.text: The specialist works for the client and may be biased toward client interests
Client specialists are always more skilled
Objectivity is irrelevant for client specialists

questions.explanation: Correct: A. The specialist works for the client and may be biased toward client interests

questions.prompt: The specialist’s conclusions are inconsistent with other audit evidence. The auditor should:

choices.text: Resolve the inconsistency, performing additional procedures if needed

questions.explanation: Correct: D. Resolve the inconsistency, performing additional procedures if needed

questions.prompt: A “specialist” is best described as a person or firm with special skill or knowledge in:

choices.text: A field other than accounting or auditing

questions.explanation: Correct: B. A field other than accounting or auditing

questions.module: Module 12: Judgment, Estimates, and Going Concern
questions.prompt: Judgments in auditing are difficult primarily because they reflect:
questions.explanation: Correct: C. Uncertainty and subjectivity

questions.module: Module 12: Judgment, Estimates, and Going Concern
questions.prompt: (Select ALL that apply.) Judgmental items are problematic because they:

choices.text: Allow people to reach differing conclusions

questions.explanation: Correct: A,B,C,D. Reflect uncertainty about future events; Reflect subjectivity; Often have little “hard” evidence; Allow people to reach differing conclusions

questions.module: Module 12: Judgment, Estimates, and Going Concern
questions.prompt: Because judgments are difficult and complex, humans tend to use:
questions.explanation: Correct: A. Heuristics

questions.module: Module 12: Judgment, Estimates, and Going Concern
questions.prompt: A heuristic is best described as:

choices.text: A mental shortcut that uses fewer cues or steps, trading accuracy for efficiency

questions.explanation: Correct: D. A mental shortcut that uses fewer cues or steps, trading accuracy for efficiency

questions.module: Module 12: Judgment, Estimates, and Going Concern
questions.prompt: (Select ALL that apply.) Synonyms or close relatives of heuristics include:
questions.explanation: Correct: A,B,C,D. Rules of thumb; Stereotypes; Educated guesses; Common sense

questions.module: Module 12: Judgment, Estimates, and Going Concern
questions.prompt: An auditor starts from last year’s materiality and adjusts only slightly despite new facts. This is:
questions.explanation: Correct: B. Anchoring and adjustment.

questions.module: Module 12: Judgment, Estimates, and Going Concern
questions.prompt: An auditor wants controls to be effective (to cut substantive work) and reads ambiguous test results favorably. This is:
questions.explanation: Correct: C. Motivated reasoning.

questions.module: Module 12: Judgment, Estimates, and Going Concern
questions.prompt: After a prior inventory fraud, an auditor overestimates inventory fraud risk at a new client with strong controls because the case is easy to recall. This is:
questions.explanation: Correct: A. Availability.

questions.module: Module 12: Judgment, Estimates, and Going Concern
questions.prompt: An auditor looks for evidence that supports her initial risk assessment and discounts contradictory evidence. This is:
questions.explanation: Correct: D. Confirmation bias.

questions.module: Module 12: Judgment, Estimates, and Going Concern
questions.prompt: Giving the most weight to the last piece of evidence received is a:
questions.explanation: Correct: B. Recency.

questions.module: Module 12: Judgment, Estimates, and Going Concern
questions.prompt: Asking “Does management show integrity?” versus “Might management act dishonestly?” leads to different conclusions on the same evidence. This is:
questions.explanation: Correct: C. Framing.

questions.module: Module 12: Judgment, Estimates, and Going Concern
questions.prompt: The dilution effect occurs when:

choices.text: Irrelevant information weakens the influence of relevant information

questions.explanation: Correct: A. Dilution.

questions.module: Module 12: Judgment, Estimates, and Going Concern
questions.prompt: (Select ALL that apply.) Which are judgment biases or heuristics?
questions.explanation: Correct: A,B,C,D. Materiality is not a bias.

questions.module: Module 12: Judgment, Estimates, and Going Concern
questions.prompt: Under AS 2501, the auditor must use:

choices.text: All three approaches in every audit
At least one of three approaches

questions.explanation: Correct: B. At least one of the three.

questions.module: Module 12: Judgment, Estimates, and Going Concern
questions.prompt: (Select ALL that apply.) The approaches in AS 2501 are:

choices.text: Evaluate evidence from events occurring after the measurement date
Rely solely on a representation letter
Confirm the estimate with the bank

questions.explanation: Correct: A,B,C. Test management’s process; Develop an independent estimate; Evaluate evidence from events occurring after the measurement date

questions.module: Module 12: Judgment, Estimates, and Going Concern
questions.prompt: To test the allowance for doubtful accounts, an auditor examines cash collected after year-end. This is which approach?

choices.text: Subsequent events (events after the measurement date)

questions.explanation: Correct: A. Subsequent events.

questions.module: Module 12: Judgment, Estimates, and Going Concern
questions.prompt: The auditor builds her own model of a fair value estimate using her own methods and data. This is:
questions.explanation: Correct: D. Independent estimate.

questions.module: Module 12: Judgment, Estimates, and Going Concern
questions.prompt: (Select ALL that apply.) Significant assumptions are those that are:

choices.text: Dependent on the company’s intent and ability to carry out a course of action

questions.explanation: Correct: A,B,C,D. Sensitive to variation; Susceptible to misstatement and bias; Based on unobservable data; Dependent on the company’s intent and ability to carry out a course of action

questions.module: Module 12: Judgment, Estimates, and Going Concern
questions.prompt: When testing management’s process, evaluating methods includes determining whether the method is:
questions.explanation: Correct: C. Appropriate and applied consistently

questions.module: Module 12: Judgment, Estimates, and Going Concern
questions.prompt: When the auditor develops an independent estimate using third-party data, the auditor should:

choices.text: Evaluate the relevance and reliability of the third-party data and test any company-provided data

questions.explanation: Correct: B. Evaluate the relevance and reliability of the third-party data and test any company-provided data

questions.module: Module 12: Judgment, Estimates, and Going Concern
questions.prompt: Under AS 2415, the auditor evaluates whether substantial doubt exists about the client’s ability to continue for a reasonable period not to exceed:
questions.explanation: Correct: C. 12 months.

questions.module: Module 12: Judgment, Estimates, and Going Concern
questions.prompt: If there is substantial doubt, the auditor reviews management’s plans and asks whether:

choices.text: Management has the ability and intent to execute it, and whether it will resolve the doubt

questions.explanation: Correct: B. Management has the ability and intent to execute it, and whether it will resolve the doubt

questions.module: Module 12: Judgment, Estimates, and Going Concern
questions.prompt: If substantial doubt remains unresolved, the auditor:

choices.text: Adds an explanatory paragraph to the audit report

questions.explanation: Correct: B. Explanatory paragraph.

questions.module: Module 12: Judgment, Estimates, and Going Concern
questions.prompt: (Select ALL that apply.) In evaluating management’s plans, the auditor considers whether:

choices.text: The plan will resolve the doubt
Management has the ability to execute it
Management has the intent to execute it
The plan has already been implemented in prior years only

questions.explanation: Correct: A,B,C. The plan will resolve the doubt; Management has the ability to execute it; Management has the intent to execute it

questions.module: Module 12: Judgment, Estimates, and Going Concern
questions.prompt: The “self-fulfilling prophecy” argument against going concern opinions is that:

choices.text: The opinion itself can cause creditors and others to withdraw support, contributing to failure

questions.explanation: Correct: D. The opinion itself can cause creditors and others to withdraw support, contributing to failure

questions.module: Module 12: Judgment, Estimates, and Going Concern
questions.prompt: Compared with AS 2415, ISA 570:

choices.text: Evaluates management’s own assessment over the same period and calls for an adverse opinion if the going concern basis is inappropriate

questions.explanation: Correct: C. Evaluates management’s own assessment over the same period and calls for an adverse opinion if the going concern basis is inappropriate

questions.prompt: The dictionary definition of fraud is the:

choices.text: Intentional use of deceit, a trick, or dishonest means to deprive another of property or legal rights

questions.explanation: Correct: B. Intentional use of deceit, a trick, or dishonest means to deprive another of property or legal rights

questions.prompt: (Select ALL that apply.) Elements of fraud from a legal standpoint include:

choices.text: A false representation of a material nature
Reliance by the person receiving the representation

questions.explanation: Correct: A,B,C,D. Negligence is not fraud.

questions.prompt: Scienter refers to:

choices.text: The mental state of intent to deceive, manipulate, or defraud

questions.explanation: Correct: C. The mental state of intent to deceive, manipulate, or defraud

questions.prompt: According to AS 2401, fraud is:

choices.text: A legal determination made by the auditor
An intentional act that results in a material misstatement in financial statements that are the subject of an audit

questions.explanation: Correct: D. An intentional act that results in a material misstatement in financial statements that are the subject of an audit

questions.prompt: With respect to fraud, the auditor:

choices.text: Does not make legal determinations but is concerned with whether misstatements are intentional (fraud) or unintentional (error)

questions.explanation: Correct: B. Does not make legal determinations but is concerned with whether misstatements are intentional (fraud) or unintentional (error)

questions.prompt: PCAOB standards describe two types of fraud:

choices.text: Fraudulent financial reporting and misappropriation of assets

questions.explanation: Correct: C. Fraudulent financial reporting and misappropriation of assets

questions.prompt: The CFO inflates revenue to meet an earnings target. This is:

choices.text: An illegal act with only direct effects

questions.explanation: Correct: A. Fraudulent financial reporting

questions.prompt: A warehouse employee steals inventory and falsifies counts to hide it. This is:
questions.explanation: Correct: D. Misappropriation of assets

questions.prompt: How does the auditor’s strategy differ between the two types?

choices.text: For financial statement fraud, management is the potential perpetrator and opposes the auditor; for employee misappropriation, management is generally on the auditor’s side

questions.explanation: Correct: B. For financial statement fraud, management is the potential perpetrator and opposes the auditor; for employee misappropriation, management is generally on the auditor’s side

questions.prompt: (Select ALL that apply.) Which statements are true?

choices.text: Fraudulent financial reporting is typically perpetrated by management
Misappropriation of assets is typically perpetrated by employees
The two types require identical audit approaches
With employee misappropriation, management is generally on the auditor’s side
Management is always on the auditor’s side

questions.explanation: Correct: A,B,D. Fraudulent financial reporting is typically perpetrated by management; Misappropriation of assets is typically perpetrated by employees; With employee misappropriation, management is generally on the auditor’s side

questions.prompt: SAS 1 (1972) indicated the auditor:

choices.text: Must search for all management fraud
Is aware that fraud may exist, but the examination is not designed to detect it
Must guarantee the absence of fraud

questions.explanation: Correct: C. SAS 1.

questions.prompt: SAS 16 (1977) introduced a responsibility to:

choices.text: Search for errors or irregularities that have a material effect on the statements

questions.explanation: Correct: A. SAS 16.

questions.prompt: SAS 53 (1988) required the auditor to:

choices.text: Assess the risk that errors and irregularities may cause material misstatement and design the audit accordingly

questions.explanation: Correct: B. SAS 53.

questions.prompt: SAS 82 (1997) is notable because it:

choices.text: Required the auditor to specifically assess fraud risk, covering both types of fraud

questions.explanation: Correct: D. SAS 82.

questions.prompt: SAS 99 (2002), now reflected in AS 2401, requires the auditor to:

choices.text: Plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance of detecting material misstatement due to fraud or error, and presume improper revenue recognition is a fraud risk

questions.explanation: Correct: A. SAS 99 / AS 2401.

questions.prompt: (Select ALL that apply.) Under AS 2401, the auditor’s current responsibility includes:

choices.text: Obtaining reasonable (not absolute) assurance about material misstatement
Considering misstatements caused by error or fraud
Presuming revenue recognition is a fraud risk
Guaranteeing that all fraud is detected
Considering the risk of management override of controls

questions.explanation: Correct: A,B,C,E. Obtaining reasonable (not absolute) assurance about material misstatement; Considering misstatements caused by error or fraud; Presuming revenue recognition is a fraud risk; Considering the risk of management override of controls

questions.prompt: “Reasonable assurance” means:

choices.text: A high but not absolute level of assurance

questions.explanation: Correct: D. A high but not absolute level of assurance

questions.prompt: The three conditions of the fraud triangle are:
questions.explanation: Correct: C. Incentive/pressure, opportunity, and rationalization/attitude

questions.prompt: (Select ALL that apply.) The fraud triangle includes:
questions.explanation: Correct: A,B,C. Incentive or pressure; Opportunity; Rationalization or attitude

questions.prompt: A CFO’s bonus depends on hitting an EPS target. This illustrates the:
questions.explanation: Correct: B. Incentive/pressure.

questions.prompt: A company has no segregation of duties and weak oversight over cash. This most directly increases:
questions.explanation: Correct: D. Opportunity.

questions.prompt: An employee who “borrows” from petty cash says, “I’ll pay it back once things improve.” This reflects:
questions.explanation: Correct: A. Rationalization.

questions.prompt: (Select ALL that apply.) During the planning discussion about fraud, the engagement team should consider:

choices.text: How the financial statements might be susceptible to material misstatement due to fraud
How management could perpetrate and conceal fraudulent financial reporting
The need to emphasize professional skepticism
How to set the audit fee

questions.explanation: Correct: A,B,C,D. How the financial statements might be susceptible to material misstatement due to fraud; How management could perpetrate and conceal fraudulent financial reporting; How assets could be misappropriated; The need to emphasize professional skepticism

questions.prompt: The primary purpose of the team’s fraud brainstorming is to:

choices.text: Share insights and heighten awareness of where and how fraud could occur

questions.explanation: Correct: C. Share insights and heighten awareness of where and how fraud could occur

questions.prompt: (Select ALL that apply.) In assessing fraud risk, the auditor makes inquiries of:
questions.explanation: Correct: A,B,C. Management; The audit committee; Internal auditors

questions.prompt: (Select ALL that apply.) Factors relevant to identifying fraud risk include:

choices.text: Events or conditions indicating a component of the fraud triangle
The presumption of fraud risk in revenue recognition
The risk of management override of controls

questions.explanation: Correct: A,B,C,D. Events or conditions indicating a component of the fraud triangle; Incomplete or inaccurate disclosure; The presumption of fraud risk in revenue recognition; The risk of management override of controls

questions.prompt: Which fraud risk must the auditor presume exists?
questions.explanation: Correct: B. Revenue recognition.

questions.prompt: Which is performed regardless of the assessed risks, to address management override?

choices.text: Examining journal entries (plus reviewing estimates for bias and unusual transactions)

questions.explanation: Correct: B. Journal entries (also estimates and unusual transactions).

questions.prompt: (Select ALL that apply.) Appropriate responses to heightened fraud risk include:

choices.text: Modifying the nature, timing, and extent of procedures
Performing analytical procedures on disaggregated data
Reducing professional skepticism to finish on time

questions.explanation: Correct: A,B,C. Modifying the nature, timing, and extent of procedures; Incorporating unpredictability; Performing analytical procedures on disaggregated data

questions.prompt: (Select ALL that apply.) For a revenue fraud risk, appropriate responses include:

choices.text: Confirming contract terms and the absence of side agreements
Inquiring of sales, marketing, and legal personnel
Being present at period-end to observe shipments

questions.explanation: Correct: A,B,C,D. Analytical procedures on disaggregated data; Confirming contract terms and the absence of side agreements; Inquiring of sales, marketing, and legal personnel; Being present at period-end to observe shipments

questions.prompt: (Select ALL that apply.) For fraud risk in accounting estimates, appropriate responses include:

choices.text: Performing a retrospective review of prior estimates

questions.explanation: Correct: A,B,C,D. Using a specialist; Developing an independent estimate; Performing a retrospective review of prior estimates; Looking for management bias

questions.prompt: An auditor suspects inventory manipulation at a remote warehouse. Which response is MOST responsive?

choices.text: Perform an unannounced observation near year-end, examine packaged inventory carefully, and consider a specialist
Inquire only of the warehouse manager

questions.explanation: Correct: B. Perform an unannounced observation near year-end, examine packaged inventory carefully, and consider a specialist

questions.prompt: Fraud involving senior management, or any material fraud, should be reported:
questions.explanation: Correct: A. Directly to the audit committee.

questions.prompt: (Select ALL that apply.) The auditor may report fraud outside the client to:

choices.text: Comply with legal and regulatory requirements
A funding agency or other specified agency

questions.explanation: Correct: A,B,C,D. Comply with legal and regulatory requirements; A successor auditor (with client permission); Respond to a subpoena; A funding agency or other specified agency

questions.prompt: (Select ALL that apply.) Fraud is difficult to find because:

choices.text: Sophisticated people (including management) can perpetrate and conceal it
It is concealed by withholding evidence, falsifying documents, side agreements, and collusion
It is hard to tell whether detected misstatements are intentional or unintentional
It always leaves an obvious trail

questions.explanation: Correct: A,B,C,D. Sophisticated people (including management) can perpetrate and conceal it; It is concealed by withholding evidence, falsifying documents, side agreements, and collusion; It is hard to tell whether detected misstatements are intentional or unintentional; It is strategic

questions.prompt: Why is fraud risk different from error risk?

choices.text: Fraud risk is easier to measure
A potential fraudster anticipates the auditor’s assessment and response and adjusts, so fraud risk is strategic

questions.explanation: Correct: D. Fraud risk is strategic.

questions.prompt: Illegal acts are violations of laws or government regulations attributable to:

choices.text: The entity, or management or employees acting on behalf of the entity

questions.explanation: Correct: C. The entity, or management or employees acting on behalf of the entity

questions.prompt: (Select ALL that apply.) Illegal acts under AS 2405 include violations by:

choices.text: Management’s personal misconduct unrelated to business activities

questions.explanation: Correct: A,B,C. The entity; Management acting on its behalf; Employees acting on its behalf

questions.prompt: Which is NOT an illegal act as defined?

choices.text: A tax law violation by the entity
An environmental violation by employees at work
Bribery by a manager to win business
Management’s personal misconduct unrelated to the business

questions.explanation: Correct: D. Management’s personal misconduct unrelated to the business

questions.prompt: Determining whether an act is illegal normally:

choices.text: Requires a legal determination outside the auditor’s professional competence

questions.explanation: Correct: A. Requires a legal determination outside the auditor’s professional competence

questions.prompt: An illegal act with a direct effect is one where the law:

choices.text: Directly and materially affects financial statement amounts

questions.explanation: Correct: B. Directly and materially affects financial statement amounts

questions.prompt: Which is MOST likely a direct-effect illegal act?

choices.text: A tax law violation that misstates the income tax accrual and expense

questions.explanation: Correct: B. Tax law violation misstating the accrual.

questions.prompt: (Select ALL that apply.) Laws whose violations typically have indirect effects include:

choices.text: Insider trading and securities trading laws
Income tax laws that determine the tax accrual

questions.explanation: Correct: A,B,C,D. Tax law is direct.

questions.prompt: For illegal acts with a direct effect, the auditor’s responsibility is:

choices.text: The same as for errors or fraud

questions.explanation: Correct: C. Same as for errors or fraud.

questions.prompt: For illegal acts with an indirect effect, the audit is:

choices.text: Designed to detect all of them
Required to confirm every law with regulators
Not normally designed to detect them, and no assurance is provided that they will be detected

questions.explanation: Correct: D. Not normally designed to detect them, and no assurance is provided that they will be detected

questions.prompt: What assurance does the auditor provide that liabilities arising from indirect-effect illegal acts will be recorded and disclosed?

choices.text: No assurance that such contingent liabilities will be recorded

questions.explanation: Correct: A. No assurance.

questions.prompt: (Select ALL that apply.) Information that may indicate an illegal act has occurred includes:

choices.text: Unauthorized transactions or improperly recorded transactions
An investigation by a governmental agency or enforcement proceeding
Large payments for unspecified services to consultants, affiliates, or employees
Unexplained payments to government officials or employees

questions.explanation: Correct: A,B,C,D. Unauthorized transactions or improperly recorded transactions; An investigation by a governmental agency or enforcement proceeding; Large payments for unspecified services to consultants, affiliates, or employees; Unexplained payments to government officials or employees

questions.prompt: Which procedure does the auditor specifically perform regarding illegal acts?

choices.text: Inquiring of management about their knowledge of illegal acts
Hiring an investigator for every audit

questions.explanation: Correct: B. Inquiring of management about their knowledge of illegal acts

questions.prompt: (Select ALL that apply.) Audit procedures that may make the auditor aware of illegal acts include:

choices.text: Reading minutes of board and committee meetings
Substantive tests of transactions and balances

questions.explanation: Correct: A,B,C,D. Inquiring of management; Reading minutes of board and committee meetings; Inquiring of legal counsel; Substantive tests of transactions and balances

questions.prompt: The auditor believes an illegal act with a material indirect effect may have occurred. The auditor should:

choices.text: Ignore it unless it is a tax issue
Attempt to determine whether it occurred, including consulting the client’s legal counsel or other specialists and applying additional procedures

questions.explanation: Correct: D. Attempt to determine whether it occurred, including consulting the client’s legal counsel or other specialists and applying additional procedures

questions.prompt: (Select ALL that apply.) Additional procedures to understand a possible illegal act include:

choices.text: Confirming significant information with the other party
Determining whether the transaction was properly authorized
Considering whether similar transactions may have occurred

questions.explanation: Correct: A,B,C,D. Examining supporting documents; Confirming significant information with the other party; Determining whether the transaction was properly authorized; Considering whether similar transactions may have occurred

questions.prompt: If an illegal act has occurred, the auditor considers:

choices.text: The impact on the financial statements and whether there are related material misstatements

questions.explanation: Correct: A. The impact on the financial statements and whether there are related material misstatements

questions.prompt: The auditor should report illegal acts to:

choices.text: The audit committee (those charged with governance) or the board of directors

questions.explanation: Correct: C. The audit committee (those charged with governance) or the board of directors

questions.prompt: The client does not respond appropriately to an illegal act. The auditor should consider:

choices.text: Withdrawing from the engagement and the effect on the audit report

questions.explanation: Correct: B. Withdrawing from the engagement and the effect on the audit report

questions.prompt: (Select ALL that apply.) If the client does not take appropriate action, the auditor should consider:

choices.text: The effect on the audit report (qualification, adverse opinion, or disclaimer)
Informing the audit committee or board
Ignoring the matter if the client objects

questions.explanation: Correct: A,B,C. The effect on the audit report (qualification, adverse opinion, or disclaimer); Withdrawing from the engagement; Informing the audit committee or board

questions.prompt: How does the auditor’s responsibility for indirect-effect illegal acts differ from that for fraud?

choices.text: Fraud is never the auditor’s responsibility
Illegal acts are always tested directly
For fraud the auditor must plan to obtain reasonable assurance; for indirect-effect illegal acts the audit is not designed to detect them and provides no assurance

questions.explanation: Correct: D. For fraud the auditor must plan to obtain reasonable assurance; for indirect-effect illegal acts the audit is not designed to detect them and provides no assurance

questions.prompt: The PCAOB’s NOCLAR proposal would replace the term “illegal acts” with:
questions.explanation: Correct: B. Noncompliance with laws and regulations

questions.prompt: (Select ALL that apply.) The NOCLAR proposal would:

choices.text: Replace “illegal acts” with noncompliance with laws and regulations
Include fraud in the NOCLAR definition
Require procedures to identify laws whose noncompliance could materially affect the statements
Require assessing and responding to risks of material misstatement due to noncompliance
Eliminate the auditor’s responsibility for indirect-effect acts

questions.explanation: Correct: A,B,C,D. Replace “illegal acts” with noncompliance with laws and regulations; Include fraud in the NOCLAR definition; Require procedures to identify laws whose noncompliance could materially affect the statements; Require assessing and responding to risks of material misstatement due to noncompliance

questions.prompt: The current status of the NOCLAR proposal is that consideration has been:

choices.text: Paused (put on hold); AS 2405 remains in effect

questions.explanation: Correct: C. Paused; AS 2405 remains in effect.

questions.prompt: The auditor learns of unexplained payments to foreign officials. The best course is to:

choices.text: Report them to the SEC immediately
Inquire of management and consult legal counsel, expand procedures, evaluate the impact on the statements, and communicate with the audit committee

questions.explanation: Correct: C. Inquire of management and consult legal counsel, expand procedures, evaluate the impact on the statements, and communicate with the audit committee

questions.prompt: Which situation is an indirect-effect illegal act?

choices.text: A client dumps toxic waste in violation of environmental regulations, creating potential fines and cleanup liabilities
A client intentionally miscalculates its income tax accrual
A client’s clerical error in a ledger

questions.explanation: Correct: A. A client dumps toxic waste in violation of environmental regulations, creating potential fines and cleanup liabilities

questions.prompt: Which statement about indirect-effect illegal acts is correct?

choices.text: The auditor will always be aware of them
The auditor is unlikely to be aware of such violations unless informed by the client or a regulatory investigation

questions.explanation: Correct: B. The auditor is unlikely to be aware of such violations unless informed by the client or a regulatory investigation

questions.prompt: (Select ALL that apply.) Which of the following are tests of details (not analytical procedures)?

choices.text: Vouching a sample of sales entries to shipping documents
Confirming a sample of customer balances
Comparing gross margin percentage to the prior year
Examining invoices for a sample of repairs expense items

questions.explanation: Correct: A,B,C,E. D is an analytical procedure.

questions.prompt: Substantive analytical procedures are generally MOST effective for:

choices.text: Large volumes of transactions that tend to be predictable over time (e.g., payroll, interest)

questions.explanation: Correct: A. Predictable, high-volume items.

questions.prompt: A 120-room hotel (365 days) expects 70% occupancy at an average daily rate of $150. What is the expected room revenue?
Using the expectation in Q203, recorded room revenue is $4,750,000 and the auditor’s investigation threshold is $100,000. The auditor should:

choices.text: Investigate the $151,000 difference, because it exceeds the threshold
Accept the difference, because it is under 4% of revenue

questions.prompt: Average debt is $2,000,000 at 6%. Recorded interest expense is $150,000. The investigation threshold is $20,000. The best next step is to:

choices.text: Investigate the $30,000 difference (e.g., additional borrowings, rate changes, or misstatement) and corroborate explanations
Ask management to restate the expectation

questions.explanation: Correct: B. Expected $120,000; difference $30,000 exceeds $20,000.

questions.prompt: (Select ALL that apply.) Which factors increase the reliability of data used to form an expectation?

choices.text: Effective internal controls over the data
Data obtained from a source independent of the client
Unaudited internal budgets prepared without controls
Data from a source with an incentive to misstate

questions.explanation: Correct: A,B,C. Effective internal controls over the data; Data obtained from a source independent of the client; Data that has been audited

questions.prompt: The auditor needs a high level of assurance from the analytical procedure (low AP risk). Which expectation is most appropriate?

choices.text: A regression model incorporating several driving factors
A simple comparison to prior-year balance
An unadjusted comparison with a competitor

questions.explanation: Correct: A. More precise expectation for more assurance.

questions.prompt: Comparing gross profit percentage over time and against industry peers is an example of:
questions.explanation: Correct: C. Ratio analysis.

questions.prompt: Consolidated-level trend analysis is relatively imprecise because:

choices.text: Offsetting changes across components can mask misstatements
Trend analysis cannot be used for revenue

questions.explanation: Correct: B. Offsetting changes mask misstatements.

questions.prompt: The auditor builds the expectation for sales from the same sales ledger being tested. The main problem is:

choices.text: The data is not independent of the recorded amount, so it lacks reliability as a basis for the expectation

questions.explanation: Correct: A. The expectation must be independent of the recorded amount.

questions.prompt: (Select ALL that apply.) After finding a significant difference between expectation and recorded amount, the auditor should:

choices.text: Consider plausible explanations other than misstatement
Perform additional procedures if the difference is not explained
Change the expectation to equal the recorded amount

questions.explanation: Correct: A,B,C,D. Never force the expectation to match.

questions.prompt: When using industry data to build an expectation, the auditor should be most concerned with:

choices.text: The comparability and reliability of the industry data
The font used in the report

questions.explanation: Correct: A. The comparability and reliability of the industry data

questions.prompt: AuR = 5%, IR = 100%, CR = 50%, AP risk = 50%. What is the acceptable TD risk?
Using the same facts but with NO substantive analytical procedures (AP risk = 100%), the acceptable TD risk is:
Compared with relying on a strong substantive AP (AP risk = 50%), performing no substantive AP means tests of details must:

choices.text: Provide more assurance, so the TD sample will be larger
Provide less assurance, so samples shrink

questions.explanation: Correct: A. Lower acceptable TD means a larger sample.

questions.prompt: Analytical procedures performed in the planning phase:

choices.text: Are not substantive procedures; they help identify risk

questions.explanation: Correct: C. Are not substantive procedures; they help identify risk

questions.prompt: (Select ALL that apply.) Substantive analytical procedures are LESS effective when:

choices.text: The business environment is unstable and relationships are unpredictable
There are many routine transactions with stable relationships

questions.explanation: Correct: A,B,C,E. Transactions are unusual or nonrecurring; The account is highly subjective; The business environment is unstable and relationships are unpredictable; The underlying data is unreliable

questions.prompt: Which statistic indicates the precision of a regression-based expectation?

choices.text: The standard error of the estimate (with R² as a goodness-of-fit measure)

questions.explanation: Correct: C. Standard error of the estimate.

questions.prompt: An advantage of a reasonableness test over a trend analysis is that it:

choices.text: Builds an explicit expectation from related financial and nonfinancial data

questions.explanation: Correct: A. Builds an explicit expectation from related financial and nonfinancial data

questions.prompt: The auditor accepts a low-precision expectation but sets a very wide investigation threshold, and no difference is found. The auditor can conclude:

choices.text: Misstatements below the threshold are impossible
Only that no difference exceeds the threshold, with limited assurance because of low precision

questions.explanation: Correct: C. A wide threshold plus low precision gives limited assurance.

questions.prompt: (Select ALL that apply.) Which statements about precision are TRUE?

choices.text: Expectations at a lower level of aggregation are generally more precise
Objectively determined accounts allow more precise expectations
Regression is generally more precise than a simple trend
Unaudited data without controls improves precision
Higher required assurance demands greater precision

questions.explanation: Correct: A,B,C,E. Expectations at a lower level of aggregation are generally more precise; Objectively determined accounts allow more precise expectations; Regression is generally more precise than a simple trend; Higher required assurance demands greater precision

questions.prompt: Credit sales are $5,000,000 and the auditor expects bad debt expense of 2% ($100,000). Recorded expense is $60,000; tolerable difference is $15,000. The auditor should:

choices.text: Investigate the $40,000 difference, corroborate any explanation, and consider a possible understated allowance

questions.explanation: Correct: C. $100,000 − $60,000 = $40,000, above $15,000; possible understated allowance.

questions.prompt: Gross margin fell from 40% to 35% against a stable expectation. Which explanation points to a possible misstatement rather than a business cause?

choices.text: Unrecorded sales or overstated cost of goods sold

questions.explanation: Correct: B. Unrecorded sales or overstated cost of goods sold

questions.prompt: (Select ALL that apply.) To evaluate management’s explanation for unexpectedly low bad debt expense (new tighter credit policy), the auditor could:

choices.text: Review the new credit policy and its approval
Inquire of independent parties such as collections personnel
Obtain only a management representation letter

questions.explanation: Correct: A,B,C. Review the new credit policy and its approval; Obtain evidence it was implemented; Inquire of independent parties such as collections personnel

questions.prompt: Analytical procedures (AP) risk is the probability that:

choices.text: The substantive analytical procedures will not detect a material misstatement that occurred and was not prevented or detected by internal control

questions.explanation: Correct: A. The substantive analytical procedures will not detect a material misstatement that occurred and was not prevented or detected by internal control

questions.module: Module 12 bonus: Judgment, Estimates, and Going Concern
questions.prompt: (Select ALL that apply.) Judgment is involved in which phases of an audit?

choices.text: Planning (materiality, inherent and control risk assessment)

questions.explanation: Correct: A,B,C,D. Client acceptance (engagement risk); Planning (materiality, inherent and control risk assessment); Fieldwork (sample sizes, estimates); Wrap-up (going concern, sufficiency of evidence)

questions.module: Module 12 bonus: Judgment, Estimates, and Going Concern
questions.prompt: In auditing estimates, the auditor often must form:
questions.explanation: Correct: C. Judgments about management’s judgments

questions.module: Module 12 bonus: Judgment, Estimates, and Going Concern
questions.prompt: Judgmental items could provide opportunities for fraud because:

choices.text: They are hard to detect or prove to be wrong

questions.explanation: Correct: B. They are hard to detect or prove to be wrong

questions.module: Module 12 bonus: Judgment, Estimates, and Going Concern
questions.prompt: An auditor sets this year’s sample size by taking last year’s and adjusting only slightly, despite changed risks. This is:
questions.explanation: Correct: A. Anchoring and adjustment.

questions.module: Module 12 bonus: Judgment, Estimates, and Going Concern
questions.prompt: An auditor gives too much weight to the first piece of evidence encountered. This is the:
questions.explanation: Correct: D. Primacy.

questions.module: Module 12 bonus: Judgment, Estimates, and Going Concern
questions.prompt: After a training session on revenue fraud, an auditor sees revenue fraud everywhere because the training is vivid in memory. This is:
questions.explanation: Correct: B. Availability.

questions.module: Module 12 bonus: Judgment, Estimates, and Going Concern
questions.prompt: An auditor seeks only evidence supporting management’s estimate and overlooks contradictory evidence. This is:
questions.explanation: Correct: C. Confirmation bias.

questions.module: Module 12 bonus: Judgment, Estimates, and Going Concern
questions.prompt: Evaluating the same evidence as “the estimate is reasonable” versus “the estimate is unreasonable” yields different conclusions. This is the:
questions.explanation: Correct: D. Framing.

questions.module: Module 12 bonus: Judgment, Estimates, and Going Concern
questions.prompt: A long memo is mostly irrelevant detail, and the one sentence about a covenant violation receives little weight. This is the:
questions.explanation: Correct: A. Dilution.

questions.module: Module 12 bonus: Judgment, Estimates, and Going Concern
questions.prompt: (Select ALL that apply.) Which are examples of how biases can affect auditor judgments?
