choices.text: Adjusting too little from last year’s risk assessment
Overweighting vivid or easily recalled past events
Discounting evidence that contradicts an initial view
Giving too much weight to the most recent evidence
Always improving the accuracy of the conclusion

questions.explanation: Correct: A,B,C,D. Adjusting too little from last year’s risk assessment; Overweighting vivid or easily recalled past events; Discounting evidence that contradicts an initial view; Giving too much weight to the most recent evidence

questions.module: Module 12 bonus: Judgment, Estimates, and Going Concern
questions.prompt: Under budget pressure, an auditor concludes controls are effective to avoid extra testing and reads ambiguous results accordingly. This is:
questions.explanation: Correct: B. Motivated reasoning.

questions.module: Module 12 bonus: Judgment, Estimates, and Going Concern
questions.prompt: Heuristics involve a tradeoff between:
questions.explanation: Correct: C. Judgment accuracy and judgment efficiency

questions.module: Module 12 bonus: Judgment, Estimates, and Going Concern
questions.prompt: An assumption about future warranty claim rates changes the estimate dramatically with small changes. It is a significant assumption because it is:
questions.explanation: Correct: A. Sensitive to variation.

questions.module: Module 12 bonus: Judgment, Estimates, and Going Concern
questions.prompt: A fair value estimate relies on Level 3-type unobservable inputs. This is a significant assumption because it involves:
questions.explanation: Correct: D. Unobservable data.

questions.module: Module 12 bonus: Judgment, Estimates, and Going Concern
questions.prompt: (Select ALL that apply.) Which assumptions are likely to be significant?

choices.text: Management’s intent and ability to hold securities to maturity
A stable 1% rise in office supply costs
An unobservable discount rate with a large effect on value
An assumption highly sensitive to small changes
An immaterial assumption with no effect

questions.explanation: Correct: A,C,D. Intent and ability, unobservable inputs, and high sensitivity.

questions.module: Module 12 bonus: Judgment, Estimates, and Going Concern
questions.prompt: Management’s estimation process lacks controls and its model appears flawed. Which AS 2501 approach is MOST appropriate?
questions.explanation: Correct: C. Independent estimate.

questions.module: Module 12 bonus: Judgment, Estimates, and Going Concern
questions.prompt: To audit the allowance for doubtful accounts, an auditor reviews January collections on December receivables. This is:
questions.explanation: Correct: A. Subsequent events.

questions.module: Module 12 bonus: Judgment, Estimates, and Going Concern
questions.prompt: To audit a warranty reserve, the auditor reviews management’s method, historical claims data, and assumptions. This is:
questions.explanation: Correct: B. Test of management’s process.

questions.module: Module 12 bonus: Judgment, Estimates, and Going Concern
questions.prompt: (Select ALL that apply.) When testing management’s process, the auditor evaluates whether:

choices.text: The data is accurate, complete, relevant, and reliable
The auditor’s own model is superior

questions.explanation: Correct: A,B,C,D. The method is appropriate; The method is applied consistently; The data is accurate, complete, relevant, and reliable; The significant assumptions are reasonable

questions.module: Module 12 bonus: Judgment, Estimates, and Going Concern
questions.prompt: (Select ALL that apply.) The auditor checks whether significant assumptions are consistent with:

choices.text: Relevant industry, regulatory, and external factors, including economic conditions
The company’s objectives, strategies, and related business risks
Other significant assumptions used in other company estimates

questions.explanation: Correct: A,B,C,D,E. Relevant industry, regulatory, and external factors, including economic conditions; The company’s objectives, strategies, and related business risks; Existing market information; Historical or recent experience; Other significant assumptions used in other company estimates

questions.module: Module 12 bonus: Judgment, Estimates, and Going Concern
questions.prompt: When the auditor develops an independent estimate, the final step is to:

choices.text: Compare it to management’s recorded estimate and evaluate any difference

questions.explanation: Correct: A. Compare it to management’s recorded estimate and evaluate any difference

questions.module: Module 12 bonus: Judgment, Estimates, and Going Concern
questions.prompt: A client has a $3 million loan due in six months, negative cash flows, and plans to refinance. In the going concern evaluation the auditor should assess whether:

choices.text: The plan will resolve the doubt and management has the ability and intent to carry it out

questions.explanation: Correct: C. The plan will resolve the doubt and management has the ability and intent to carry it out

questions.module: Module 12 bonus: Judgment, Estimates, and Going Concern
questions.prompt: Under ISA 570, if management’s going concern assessment covers less than 12 months, the auditor:

choices.text: Requests that management extend the period

questions.explanation: Correct: D. Requests that management extend the period

questions.module: Module 12 bonus: Judgment, Estimates, and Going Concern
questions.prompt: (Select ALL that apply.) Which statements about going concern opinions are supported by the slides?

choices.text: Only about half of companies filing for bankruptcy had received going concern opinions
Some argue a going concern opinion can be a self-fulfilling prophecy
The public wonders “where was the auditor?” when companies fail
Auditors never issue going concern opinions
AS 2415 requires evaluating a period of three years

questions.explanation: Correct: A,B,C. Only about half of companies filing for bankruptcy had received going concern opinions; Some argue a going concern opinion can be a self-fulfilling prophecy; The public wonders “where was the auditor?” when companies fail

questions.module: Module 12 bonus: Judgment, Estimates, and Going Concern
questions.prompt: Which best explains why judgments are problematic?

choices.text: They reflect uncertainty and subjectivity, creating higher inherent risk and encouraging heuristics that produce biased conclusions

questions.explanation: Correct: D. They reflect uncertainty and subjectivity, creating higher inherent risk and encouraging heuristics that produce biased conclusions
